newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders debt issue for Illinois school system.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders debt issue for Illinois school system.

text.p: A U.S. District Court judge in Chicago has ordered the Rockford, Ill., school district to sell $50 million of debt in an ongoing desegregation case.

Matthew Corby, associate superintendent of management services for the school district, said Thursday that officials were working on a plan with Banc One Capital Corp to sell $50 million of certificates of participation to finance the construction of three new building to comply with the order.

He said Judge P. Michael Mahoney earlier this week ordered the borrowing as well as a tax levy to pay off the debt. The order came as result of an desegregation case originally filed against the district in 1989, Corby said.
The levy is expected to raise $4.7 million a year to pay off the COPs, which the school district hopes to insure, he said.

The school district is currently unable to issue general obligation bonds to satisfy the order because of a pending taxpayers lawsuit challenging previous tax levies for liability issues, according to Corby.

Mahoney also ordered the school district to come up with a plan to balance its budget. Corby said the district has a $15 million deficit in its $200 million fiscal 1997 budget. He said he has contacted the Illinois Department of Education to get copies of fiscal workout plans undertaken by other school districts in the state facing financial problems.

A balanced budget plan for the Rockford schools is scheduled to be presented to the school board at its Nov. 26 meeting. Corby said the board may also decide at that time whether to appeal Judge Mahoney's borrowing order.
